clue.text: Superior five-year-olds?

parts.note: children of five start school in the lowest form, so the youngest pupils are in the top-quality travel grade by a pun on school grades

explanation.surface: A question about precocious little children who are better than their peers.
explanation.walkthrough: Five-year-olds starting school go into the first class; the same phrase means top-quality, which is what 'Superior' asks for.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of the highest grade or quality is described with this phrase, which also names the opening year of primary school.

clue.text: For the climber coldly cutting in

definitions.text: For the climber coldly cutting in

parts.words: For the climber coldly cutting in
parts.note: a mountaineer's tool for chopping steps into frozen slopes, so it cuts its way into something cold

explanation.surface: Advice to a mountaineer about slicing into something in a chilly way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coldly' hints at the frozen surface and 'cutting in' at the chopping blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A mountaineer uses this pick-headed tool to chop footholds in frozen slopes.

clue.text: False and awfully unpleasant creature living by the sea

definitions.text: unpleasant creature living by the sea

indicators.note: awfully suggests the words False and are badly mangled and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone untrustworthy and very nasty lives at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awfully' reads as intensifying 'unpleasant' but rearranges the letters of FALSE AND.
explanation.definitionFit: This jumping crustacean of beaches, also called a beach flea, bites and is a nuisance.

clue.text: Offspring of a Californian prospector raising fruit

definitions.meaning: in the American folk song, the miner's daughter in the California gold rush is called this name
a small seedless citrus fruit like a mandarin

explanation.surface: A gold miner's child growing fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: In the folk song 'Oh My Darling', she is the daughter of a miner, a forty-niner, in a California canyon.
explanation.definitionFit: The song's heroine is a gold-rush miner's daughter, and the same name belongs to a small orange citrus.

clue.text: Dry wine is a sine qua non for the jet set

definitions.text: a sine qua non for the jet set

parts.note: to air clothes is to dry them
port is a fortified Portuguese wine

explanation.surface: Dry wine is essential for wealthy international travellers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dry' looks like an adjective for the wine but is the verb AIR.
explanation.definitionFit: Jet-setters cannot fly without a terminal for planes, so it is their indispensable requirement.

clue.text: Pole gone to get some pudding

parts.note: S stands for south, one of the earth's poles
ago means past or gone by

explanation.surface: A Polish person leaves to fetch a dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a Polish person but is the South Pole, S.
explanation.definitionFit: Starchy grains from a palm are cooked with milk into a milk pudding.

clue.text: Flimsy stuff possibly sags more

indicators.note: possibly signals that sags more may be rearranged into a different word

explanation.surface: Something flimsy might droop even further.
explanation.definitionFit: Fine filmy cobweb threads, or any delicate gauzy material, are proverbially flimsy.

clue.text: Written by the boy friend himself

parts.note: per means by, as in 'per post'
a son is a boy
an ally is a friend

explanation.surface: A letter penned by a boyfriend with his own hand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Written' only sets the letter scene; 'boy friend' is two pieces, not a boyfriend. 'himself' stands for doing something in person.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something oneself, without a deputy, is doing it in person.

clue.text: Left a retiring fellow in a corner

indicators.note: retiring means drawing back, so the letters for 'Left a' are read in the opposite direction

parts.note: cove is old British slang for a man or chap

explanation.surface: A shy man was left sitting in a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' looks like it describes the shy fellow, but it turns LA (L for Left plus A) round into AL. COVE is dated British slang for a fellow.
explanation.definitionFit: A recess set back in a wall is a nook, the kind of snug corner of a room.

clue.text: Drunken diner — always a real beast

indicators.note: someone drunken staggers about, so the letters of diner are jumbled

parts.note: e'er is the poetic contraction of ever, meaning always

explanation.surface: A diner who is always drunk behaves like an animal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunken' rearranges DINER into REIND; E'ER is the poetic form of 'ever'. 'real' contrasts the Arctic animal with the 'beast' that a drunk diner might be called.
explanation.definitionFit: The caribou of the Arctic is a genuine animal, unlike the insulting 'beast' a drunk might be called.

clue.text: Complains, though not against checks being made

parts.note: pro means in favour of, the opposite of against
tests are checks or trials

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles even while saying they are not against inspections being carried out.
explanation.definitionFit: To object or make a formal objection is to grumble about something publicly.

clue.text: A tiny room, only a hundred by forty-five inches!

parts.note: C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
the English ell was an old cloth measure of 45 inches

explanation.surface: A complaint that a room is cramped, measuring only a hundred by forty-five inches.
explanation.walkthrough: The ell is an old English measure of cloth, 45 inches long; 'by' sits between the pieces as if giving room dimensions.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner's or monk's small bare chamber is a tiny room.

clue.text: Set to draw up article with all-round protection

indicators.note: all-round says the protective covering goes right round the other pieces

parts.note: having a protective layer means being coated
a is the indefinite article

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the word draw is read from the bottom upward

parts.note: to lug is to drag or draw

explanation.surface: Ready to bring forward an item with full protection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Set' looks like a noun or a verb of placing, but means thickened; 'up' reverses the word for draw since this is a down clue, and 'all-round' wraps the coating round the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Blood or sauce that has set has thickened from liquid into a semi-solid mass.

clue.text: The caretaker of a growing concern

definitions.text: The caretaker of a growing concern

parts.words: The caretaker of a growing concern
parts.note: a growing concern sounds like a thriving business, but here it is a place where young plants and trees are raised and tended

explanation.surface: Someone who looks after an expanding business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'growing concern' suggests a booming firm; literally it is a business that grows plants.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who runs or works in a plant nursery raises and cares for young plants for sale.

clue.text: Men on a diet may well produce some improvement

indicators.note: may well produce suggests the words Men on a diet can be rearranged to make something new

explanation.surface: Men who diet could well see their health get better.
explanation.walkthrough: The anagram signal 'may well produce' reads as a forecast about slimmers.
explanation.definitionFit: A correction to a text, the changing of an error, is an improvement to it.

clue.text: Indoor pools for underwater swimmers

parts.note: the swimmers are fish living under water, and the indoor pools are glass tanks for keeping them

explanation.surface: Indoor swimming baths used by divers who swim beneath the surface.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests human divers training in a leisure centre; the swimmers are fish in tanks.
explanation.definitionFit: Tanks or buildings in which fish and water creatures are kept and displayed are plural water vessels of this name.

clue.text: Not in the majority as yet

definitions.text: Not in the majority as yet

parts.words: Not in the majority as yet
parts.note: majority here is the legal age of adulthood, not the larger part of a group

explanation.surface: Belonging to the minority view so far.
explanation.walkthrough: 'majority' suggests the greater number of voters; it is the age at which one legally becomes an adult.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who has not reached legal adulthood is too young for the law's purposes.

clue.text: A raptor is among the weakest, relatively speaking

indicators.note: is among says the letters sit within the run of the next words of the clue

explanation.surface: A bird of prey is one of the feebler ones, comparatively speaking.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer runs across 'weaKEST RELatively'; 'speaking' just rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This small falcon, known for hovering, is a bird of prey.

clue.text: Judge holding a mum is of less value

indicators.note: holding means containing, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a trier is one who tries a case, a judge
mum as in silent, signalled by sh, the call for quiet

explanation.surface: A judge who has a mother is considered less worthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like a mother but means silent, as in 'keep mum'; SH asks for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Something more trashy is more worthless and cheap, poorer in quality.

clue.text: Supporting occupation?

definitions.meaning: propping up, as stays brace a mast or a corset
remaining or residing in a place, occupying it

explanation.definitionFit: Ropes called stays brace a mast, and a guest's stopping somewhere is their residence.

clue.text: Champion, age not revealed, appearing without fee maybe

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece sits around another

parts.note: something undated has no date on it, so its age is not shown

indicators.note: maybe suggests the word fee could be some other arrangement of its letters

explanation.surface: A champion whose age is kept secret appears without charging a fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the old sense of outside, not lacking; 'maybe' shuffles the word fee before it goes inside. 'Champion' works as an adjective here, never beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A champion is someone never beaten, holding the title against every challenger.

clue.text: A direction to be off!

parts.note: a way is a direction or route, as in 'which way?'

explanation.surface: An instruction telling someone to leave.
explanation.walkthrough: As an exclamation the answer is a command to be gone, so 'be off!' defines it.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an exclamation, the word orders someone to go or leave at once.

clue.text: Charm a Greek character and suffer for it

parts.note: mu is the twelfth letter of the Greek alphabet
to suffer in the old sense is to allow or let

explanation.surface: Delight a Greek person and pay the price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suffer' is the old sense of allow, as in 'suffer the little children'.
explanation.definitionFit: A trinket worn to ward off evil is a lucky charm or talisman.

clue.text: Distress occasioned about a border plant

indicators.note: about means around, so one word goes round the other

parts.note: agony is extreme distress or suffering
a rim is an edge or border

explanation.surface: Someone is upset over a plant growing in a border.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border plant' reads as a garden phrase, but 'border' gives RIM and 'plant' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This yellow-flowered herb of the rose family is a wild hedgerow plant.

clue.text: There's nothing to make one unsettled

parts.note: O is zero, the figure for nothing
to wed is to unite two people as one

explanation.surface: Nothing can make a person feel disturbed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unsettled' looks like feeling uneasy, but means a bill not yet paid.
explanation.definitionFit: A debt still due has not been paid off, so the account remains unsettled.

clue.text: Letters of identification

parts.note: not documents proving who you are, but the first letters of your names used to mark your property or sign

explanation.surface: Documents that prove who someone is.
explanation.definitionFit: The first letter of each of a person's names, used as a signature or monogram, identify them.

clue.text: Commission from book

definitions.meaning: to commission someone is to hire them for work
to book is to reserve a seat or room in advance

explanation.definitionFit: The verb means both to hire someone for a job and to reserve something, like a table or a hall.

clue.text: Base of French groups, note

parts.note: de is French for of
genera are biological groups, plural of genus
te is the seventh note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: The foundation of some French groups, a note says.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Base' looks like a noun meaning foundation, but it is the adjective meaning low or depraved.
explanation.definitionFit: A base person is morally low and corrupt, someone who has sunk from a former standard.
